A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Log Probability Tracking of LLM APIs and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-C. Textual and visual inspection supports reliable comparison of the methods, equations, results, and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original TinyChange experiments, monitoring of 189 API endpoints, and additional empirical results in Appendices A-C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TinyChange experiments, API-monitoring outcomes, and appendix results. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 2.3 retains the same first-token sampling, missing-logprob imputation, mean absolute distance statistic, and permutation test. No algorithm component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LMSYS-Chat-1M data, five-model TinyChange coverage, MMLU abstract-algebra questions, and monitoring of 189 endpoints across ten providers. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: MET and MMLU-ALG remain the evaluated comparators in Section 3, Figure 4, and Table 1. Their participation and definitions are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sampling budgets, temperatures, model configurations, evaluation metrics, and preprocessing remain unchanged. Real-world monitoring still uses hourly queries and adjacent 24-sample windows with the same detection thresholds.

E4.justification: The prompt-length analysis in Figure 3, modification-sensitivity analysis in Figure 4, provider examples in Appendix B, and LoRA update analysis in Appendix C are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains 2,000 bootstraps; Figure 4 and Table 1 retain 95% confidence intervals from 10,000 bootstraps at their respective aggregation levels. Hypothesis-test repetition counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains AUCs of 0.915 for LT, 0.878 for MMLU-ALG, and 0.670 for MET, with identical intervals and costs. Table 2 still reports 37 suspected changes. All plotted results and appendix measurements, including Table 3, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8 and their associated reasoning are unchanged, including the two-sample statistics and Appendix C's singular-value argument for smaller LoRA updates. No formal assumption, definition, or derivation is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: first-token logprob auditing, detection of single-step fine-tuning, approximately 1,000-fold lower monitoring cost, and the TinyChange benchmark.

C2.justification: Interpretations of detection sensitivity, deployment changes, and LoRA update size are unchanged. Section 4 retains the same limitations concerning logprob availability, evasion, obstruction, first-token blind spots, and inability to identify a change's cause.

D1.justification: New Section 8 identifies GENCI/IDRIS and Jean Zay's H100 partition as computing and storage resources. This adds limited resource provenance; v1 already specified nodes with two H100 80GB GPUs. Implementation details and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Reference reflow and new funding acknowledgments do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and an ICLR 2026 publication header, removes advisor and correspondence annotations, and relocates the existing code notice to the first-page footnote. Scientific prose and narrative organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Repeated conference headers and limited front-matter, paragraph, and bibliography reflow alter the layout. Footnote markers on pages 5 and 9 disappear while their notes remain. All 15 figures and three tables retain their content, structure, and captions.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical evidence, theory, and limitations remain unchanged, including all appendices. Added acknowledgments and computing provenance modestly improve attribution, while missing footnote markers slightly weaken navigation. These limited documentation and presentation effects leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
